children: Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, with news expected as soon as December or in early 2027. Boards are reviewing governance and a share-swap ratio; no deal is confirmed.
Tesla invited selected customers to preorder the two-seat Cybercab, with deliveries estimated to begin in December. Public sales are planned by late 2026, subject to regulatory approval.
- Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) reported 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions in the third quarter, up from 1.04 million a year earlier. GAAP operating income declined to $718 million from $1.62 billion.
U.S. safety regulators asked Tesla to explain how its steering-wheel-free Cybercabs meet safety rules. Tesla has not sought an exemption for limited deployment.
Tesla removed its $41,990 Model Y AWD from U.S. orders. The cheapest AWD option is now the $49,990 Premium; the $39,990 rear-wheel-drive model remains available.
A proposed Tesla-SpaceX tie-up could give Tesla access to SpaceX’s Texas AI data center and enable technology sharing in autonomy, robotics and energy storage.
Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) and SpaceX are jointly building Terafab, a chip plant in Texas. Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting is scheduled for December 3.
Freedom Capital strategist Jay Woods said a Tesla-SpaceX merger could face political and regulatory hurdles if Democrats control Congress in 2027, adding that the companies are distinct businesses.
Woods raised concerns about Tesla’s future plans, citing a report that Cybertruck production stopped as the company shifts toward robotics, with few details on production or revenue.
Finland cleared Tesla’s Assisted Driving system after recognizing Dutch provisional approval. Drivers remain responsible; continuous speeding is barred, and speed settings must reset after a restart.
